name: C. Karen Liu
title: Professor of Computer Science
research_topics: Building generative models for motion synthesis or control
Experimenting with humanoids, robot arms, exoskeletons and dexterous hands
Training virtual agents using RL and transfer to real robots
Collecting data with different motion capture systems
Pre-training or fine-tuning VLMs for policy development
Solving both convex and non-convex optimization problems
Analyzing, simulating and understanding human interaction with assistive devices and robots
current_direction: Humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation learned from motion tracking
Motion retargeting and scalable teleoperated humanoid data collection
Diffusion- and flow-based generative policies for real robot control
Generative foundation models for human gait and clinical biomechanics
current_direction_basis: Driven by the 2026 items collected here, not the older graphics-centric bio. Humanoid loco-manipulation + motion tracking: BeyondMimic (2026), RPL (2026), and the 2025 OmniRetarget/ResMimic/VisualMimic arXiv line in OpenAlex. Retargeting + data collection: 'Retargeting Matters' (ICRA 2026) and TWIST2 (ICRA 2026), both first-listed on the lab's own publications feed. Generative/flow policies: 'Flow Policy Gradients for Robot Control' (2026) and BeyondMimic's guided-diffusion controller. Dexterous/muscle control: MUSIC (ACM TOG, 2026) and the lab's SimToolReal highlight. Biomechanics: GaitDynamics in Nature Biomedical Engineering (2026) plus the 2026 IEEE TBME balance-perturbation paper. The two open recruitment postings (2026-04-16, 2026-06-09) independently confirm the push toward long-horizon reasoning and human-robot physical collaboration.

evidence.title: BeyondMimic: From motion tracking to versatile humanoid control via guided diffusion
evidence.summary: Liao*, Truong*, Huang*, Gao, Tevet, Sreenath†, Liu† - turns motion tracking into general-purpose humanoid control using guided diffusion. Featured as a lab highlight; OpenAlex records a Science Robotics version dated 2026-08-26 (DOI 10.1126/scirobotics.adx8924) while the lab's own feed lists it as 'arXiv Preprint 2026' dated 2026-07-12.

evidence.title: TWIST2: Scalable, Portable, and Holistic Humanoid Data Collection System
evidence.summary: Ze, Zhao, Wang, Kanazawa, Duan, Abbeel, Shi, Wu, C. Karen Liu. Lab-listed date 2026-06-01. A whole-body teleoperation/data-collection system for humanoids; also carried as a front-page lab highlight.

evidence.title: Retargeting Matters: General Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Motion Tracking
evidence.summary: Araujo*, Ze*, Xu*, Wu†, Liu†. Lab-listed date 2026-06-01. Shows retargeting quality is a first-order factor in humanoid motion tracking. Also on OpenAlex as an arXiv preprint dated 2025-10-02.

evidence.title: Flow Policy Gradients for Robot Control
evidence.summary: Yi*, Choi*, Singh, Huang, Truong, Sferrazza, Ma, Duan†, Abbeel†, Shi†, Liu†, Kanazawa†. Lab-listed date 2026-07-13. Policy-gradient learning with flow-based generative policies for robot control.

evidence.title: RPL: Learning Robust Humanoid Perceptive Locomotion on Challenging Terrains
evidence.summary: Zhang, Seo, Chen, Yuan, Sreenath, Abbeel†, Sferrazza†, Liu†, Shi†. Lab-listed date 2026-07-13. Perception-driven humanoid locomotion over difficult terrain.

evidence.summary: Tan, Van Wouwe, Werling, Liu, Delp, Hicks, Chaudhari. Lab-listed date 2026-02-01. A generative foundation model for human gait analysis - the biomechanics/clinical arm of the lab.

recruiting.statement: VERIFIED 2026-08-31 by re-fetch. tml.stanford.edu is a JS SPA (empty <div id="root">), so the Join copy was read from the site's own Vite bundle /assets/index-CCVDOZ9A.js and the two recruitment JSONs were fetched directly at HTTP 200. Verbatim, present-tense open-recruiting text: (1) 'We are looking for researchers, engineers, and dreamers who want to shape the future of embodied intelligence.' (2) 'Thanks for your interest in joining TML! Research in our lab typically involves:' (3) 'If you are interested in working at TML, please fill out the research application form (Stanford email required).' (4) Heading 'Open Project Opportunities:' followed by two live postings. The newer, 'Gesture-Based Physical Collaboration with Humanoid Robots' (date 2026-06-09, contact Takara Truong), opens verbatim: '[Looking for students this summer continuing through the school year]' and continues 'Students will work on problems at the intersection of human-robot interaction, loco-manipulation, perception, control, simulation, and vision-language-action models'. The older is 'Reasoning and Planning for Long-Horizon Robotic Tasks' (date 2026-04-16, contact Guy Tevet). RENDER CONFIRMED: the bundle's recruitment loader statically imports exactly these two JSONs (gesture-based-physical-collaboration-with-humanoid-robots.json, reasoning-and-planning-for-long-horizon-robotic-tasks.json), sorts them by date descending, and applies NO expiry/date filter; the fallback string 'No specific projects are actively recruiting at this exact moment, but we are always looking for great talent.' is guarded by length===0 and therefore does NOT render today. LIMIT ON DEGREE LEVEL: neither posting, and no sentence in the Join copy, contains the word 'undergraduate' or any degree level. The word 'undergrad' occurs 9 times in the whole bundle and every occurrence is a People-roster role value, never recruiting copy. The only stated eligibility gate is 'Stanford email required'. UNVERIFIABLE CHANNEL: the linked research application form (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSco1zVV16lgR7W8PYC6yv9ENUUNyB0VYxYyGt7us_VddDDmYA/viewform) returns HTTP 401 behind a Google sign-in wall ('You must sign in to access this content'), consistent with a Stanford-domain restriction but NOT openable by this check - so it could not be confirmed to be still accepting responses. Both postings also name a direct human contact, which does not depend on that form. Application caveat quoted verbatim: 'Your submission will be reviewed by current TML members-typically those you indicate in the form. We will contact you in two weeks if your background interests align with ongoing projects. Due to the high volume of applications received, we regret that we are unable to respond to all submissions.'

state_rationale: OPENING upheld on adversarial re-check 2026-08-31, but at reduced confidence (0.9 -> 0.7). WHAT IS PROVEN: the lab is unambiguously and present-tense recruiting. Two dated project postings were fetched directly at HTTP 200 today, and the site bundle's recruitment loader was read to confirm they are the entire collection, are sorted by date with no expiry filter, and therefore actually render - the 'no specific projects are actively recruiting' fallback is guarded by length===0 and does not display. The newer posting (2026-06-09, contact Takara Truong) states verbatim '[Looking for students this summer continuing through the school year]'; the older is dated 2026-04-16 (contact Guy Tevet). The Join page additionally carries a standing open call: 'If you are interested in working at TML, please fill out the research application form (Stanford email required).' None of the failure modes that force a downgrade are present: there is no PhD-only funnel, no 'not taking students' statement, and this is not a bare contact page. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: no statement anywhere on the site is addressed to undergraduates. The postings say 'students' with no degree level, and the word 'undergrad' appears in the bundle only as a People-roster role, never in recruiting copy. Undergraduate relevance therefore rests on non-exclusion (the sole stated gate is a Stanford email, which an undergraduate has) plus strong circumstantial roster evidence: nine current members carry the role 'Undergrad', each with a named graduate mentor, and one of them (Yu Ding) appears in the author string of the lab's 2026 MUSIC paper. OUTSTANDING CAVEAT: the linked Google application form returns HTTP 401 behind a sign-in wall, consistent with the advertised Stanford-domain restriction but not openable here, so it could not be confirmed to be still accepting responses. Both postings name a direct human contact, so the opportunity does not depend solely on that form. A student should treat this as a real, currently-open lab-level call that welcomes undergraduates in practice, not as an undergraduate-specific program, and should expect the lab's own stated caveat that it 'cannot respond to all submissions'.
fetch_notes: DIRECTORY LINK DEAD: the supplied https://cs.stanford.edu/people/karen-liu returns HTTP 404 ('The requested URL /people/karen-liu was not found on this server'). https://cs.stanford.edu/people/c-karen-liu and /person/c-karen-liu also 404. Used https://profiles.stanford.edu/c-karen-liu (HTTP 200) as faculty_url; it confirms the title 'Professor of Computer Science' verbatim. LAB DISCOVERY: the Links section of that profile gives https://cs.stanford.edu/~karenliu, which 302-redirects to https://tml.stanford.edu/ - The Movement Lab. LAB SITE IS A JAVASCRIPT SPA: tml.stanford.edu serves an empty <div id="root"> shell for every path (including /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml, which return the same HTML), so curling page URLs yields only the title 'The Movement Lab'. Content was recovered two ways: (a) downloading the Vite bundle /assets/index-CCVDOZ9A.js (1.8 MB) and reading the inlined content modules, and (b) fetching the underlying JSON files directly at https://tml.stanford.edu/content/<collection>/<slug>.json, which the server does return as raw JSON. Both were used and agree. Routes are hash-based (#people, #publications, #courses, #join), so the '#'-anchored URLs above are the correct human-visitable addresses. RECRUITING NUANCE: the bundle contains the string 'No specific projects are actively recruiting at this exact moment, but we are always looking for great talent.' I checked the render guard before relying on it - it is wrapped in 'n.length===0 && ...', i.e. it only displays when the recruitment collection is empty. The collection currently has two entries (dated 2026-04-16 and 2026-06-09), so that message does not render for a visitor today. I did not treat it as evidence of a closed lab, and the state_rationale records both readings. NO EMAIL FOUND: regex search for email addresses returned zero hits across the full lab JS bundle, the Stanford Profiles HTML, and the profile's publications tab. email and email_source_url are therefore null - no address was guessed. OPENALEX NAME COLLISION: the filtered query authors?search=C. Karen Liu&filter=last_known_institutions.ror:00f54p054 returned count=0, so an unfiltered search was used. Five distinct 'Karen Liu' records exist; A5048338914 (143 works, Stanford) is the right one, but it is a dirty merge - its display_name_alternatives include 'Cheng Liu'/'Chengbing Liu' and its 2025+ works include 'Simulation Analysis of Thermal Deformation and Extruded Profile Formability of Al-10Mg-3Zn Aluminum Alloy' (Materials, 2026) affiliated to the Institute of New Materials. That paper is NOT hers and was excluded; every evidence item below was cross-checked against the lab's own publications feed or its explicit author list. DATE DISCREPANCY: BeyondMimic is dated 2026-07-12 / 'arXiv Preprint 2026' on the lab feed but 2026-08-26 in Science Robotics per OpenAlex (DOI 10.1126/scirobotics.adx8924); both are recorded in the evidence summary rather than silently picking one. COURSE CAVEAT: the lab's CS 123 record carries active:false with last_offered 'Fall 2025', while Stanford Profiles lists CS 123 (Aut) under 2025-26 courses - noted in the evidence item rather than resolved.
